literature.headline_zh: 人肠道病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期人肠道病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: IMB-A3 治疗 降低了受感染细胞和小鼠肌肉中的 EV-A71 VP1 蛋白和病毒 RNA 水平。在体内,IMB-A3 有效保护小鼠免受致命的 EV-A71 感染。从机制上讲,IMB-A3 促进 2C 和 CRBN 之间的相互作用,促进 2C 蛋白 N 末端区域的泛素化和降解。 [10.1016/j.antiviral.2026.106496]
时空分析显示,2017年后,283A在全球范围内取代了283T,而较小的变体(例如30D、97I、174A)则表现出局部循环。 [10.1099/jgv.0.002306]
两剂灭活 EV-D68 鼻内引发有效诱导粘膜和全身免疫。三剂量方案进一步增强了 疫苗 特异性免疫力,酵母聚糖放大了两种配方中的反应并增强了血清中和。 [10.1093/jimmun/vkag141.057]
EV-D68中和抗体血清流行率较高(>85%),绝大多数参与者(97%)在48周内表现出稳定或降低的滴度,导致几何平均滴度(GMT)总体显着降低,p<0.001;然而,6/194 (3%) 参与者的滴度显着增加(≥4 倍),GMT 从 21 (10-57) 上升至 593 (57-7241)。 [10.1016/j.ijid.2026.109008]
丙氨酸扫描显示,只有W94A几乎消除了CVA10感染,结构分析表明KRM1 W94与病毒VP2残基K140发生π-阳离子相互作用;CRISPR 工程小鼠 Krm1 W94A 突变小鼠对 CVA10 感染具有完全抵抗力。 [10.1128/mbio.01123-26]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: IMB-A3 treatment reduced EV-A71 VP1 protein and viral RNA levels in infected cells and mice muscles. In vivo, IMB-A3 effectively protected mice from lethal EV-A71 infection. [10.1016/j.antiviral.2026.106496]
A spatiotemporal analysis showed that 283A replaced 283T on a global scale after 2017, while minor variants (e.g. 30D, 97I, 174A) exhibited localized circulation. [10.1099/jgv.0.002306]

Two doses of inactivated EV-D68 with intranasal priming effectively induced mucosal and systemic immunity. A three-dose regimen further strengthened vaccine-specific immunity, with zymosan amplifying responses in both formulations and enhancing serum neutralization. [10.1093/jimmun/vkag141.057]

EV-D68 neutralizing antibody seroprevalence was high (>85%), with the vast majority of participants (97%) showing stable or reduced titers over 48 weeks, resulting in a statistically significant overall reduction in geometric mean titer (GMT), p<0.001; however, 6/194 (3%) participants had a marked increase in titers (≥4-fold), with GMT rising from 21 (10-57) to 593 (57-7241). [10.1016/j.ijid.2026.109008]

Coxsackievirus B5 was associated with an increased risk of islet autoimmunity (OR 2.22, 95% CI 1.29–3.80, p = 0.004, corrected p = 0.024), with the association remaining after adjustment for HLA, sex, and maternal type 1 diabetes. [10.1002/dmrr.70207]
literature.trend_or_risk_en: The direction of this week's research is defined by the clinical, epidemiological, ecological, diagnostic and molecular topics actually represented by the eligible publications.
literature.brief_en: This literature brief prioritizes papers published in the active reporting window and ranks them by relevance, evidence availability, study quality, recency, and independent-source convergence. Detailed study-specific evidence is retained in the article cards below.
brief_items_zh: 本期人肠道病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。

papers.title: IMB-A3, an isoindolinone derivative, functions as a molecular glue to promote CRBN-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of enterovirus A71 2C protein.
papers.abstract: EV-A71 is one of the main culprits causing hand-foot-mouth disease in children. Currently, there are no specific drugs for the prevention and treatment of EV-A71 infection. In our previous studies, a series of 2-aryl-isoindolin-1-one compounds were found to exhibit anti-EV-A71 activity, among which IMB-A3 demonstrated the most potent antiviral activity. Here, we systematically characterized the in vitro and in vivo antiviral efficacy of IMB-A3 and investigated its mechanism of action. The results showed that IMB-A3 treatment decreased the levels of EV-A71 VP1 protein and viral RNA in the infected cells and mice muscles. IMB-A3 could effectively protected mice from lethal EV-A71 infection. Mechanism studies have shown that IMB-A3 interacts directly with the EV-A71 2C protein, but IMB-A3 has no effect on the ATPase and helicase activities of the 2C protein. Interestingly, IMB-A3 acts as a molecular glue to facilitate the interaction between 2C and CRBN, thereby promoting the ubiquitination and degradation of the N-terminal region of the 2C protein and exerting an antiviral effect. These findings indicate that IMB-A3 is a degrader of the EV-A71 2C protein, providing a basis for the future design and development of targeted degraders of the EV-A71 2C protein.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) is a major cause of hand-foot-mouth disease in children, and there are currently no specific antiviral drugs available for its prevention or treatment. The study aimed to address this unmet need by systematically characterizing the antiviral efficacy and mechanism of action of IMB-A3, a compound previously shown to exhibit anti-EV-A71 activity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study characterized the in vitro and in vivo antiviral efficacy of IMB-A3 and investigated its mechanism of action. It included experiments in infected cells and mice muscles, as well as lethal EV-A71 infection models in mice.
analysis.methods: The study assessed the effects of IMB-A3 on EV-A71 VP1 protein and viral RNA levels in infected cells and mice muscles. Mechanism studies evaluated the direct interaction between IMB-A3 and the EV-A71 2C protein, its impact on 2C protein activities, and its role in promoting CRBN-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of the 2C protein.
analysis.main_results: IMB-A3 treatment reduced EV-A71 VP1 protein and viral RNA levels in infected cells and mice muscles. In vivo, IMB-A3 effectively protected mice from lethal EV-A71 infection. Mechanistically, IMB-A3 facilitated the interaction between 2C and CRBN, promoting ubiquitination and degradation of the N-terminal region of the 2C protein.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that IMB-A3 acts as a molecular glue degrader of the EV-A71 2C protein, providing a mechanistic basis for its antiviral activity. This represents a novel approach to targeting EV-A71 by inducing targeted protein degradation rather than inhibiting enzymatic function.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study identifies IMB-A3 as a promising candidate for the development of targeted antiviral therapies against EV-A71, potentially addressing the current lack of specific treatments. Its mechanism of action suggests broader applicability for designing degraders of viral proteins.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to in vitro and mouse models, which may not fully recapitulate human infection dynamics or safety profiles. While the mechanism is well-characterized, further studies are needed to evaluate efficacy, pharmacokinetics, and safety in humans before clinical translation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated IMB-A3, an isoindolinone derivative, as a potential antiviral against enterovirus A71 (EV-A71), a leading cause of hand-foot-mouth disease in children for which no specific treatments exist. The research systematically evaluated IMB-A3's antiviral efficacy in vitro and in vivo, demonstrating its ability to reduce viral protein and RNA levels in infected cells and protect mice from lethal EV-A71 infection. Mechanistic analyses revealed that IMB-A3 functions as a molecular glue, facilitating CRBN-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of the EV-A71 2C protein without inhibiting its ATPase or helicase activities. This targeted protein degradation approach represents a novel strategy for antiviral development. The findings highlight IMB-A3's potential as a lead compound for future drug design, though the current evidence is confined to preclinical models and requires validation in human studies.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) is a major cause of hand-foot-mouth disease in children, and there are currently no specific antiviral drugs available for its prevention or treatment. The study aimed to address this unmet need by systematically characterizing the antiviral efficacy and mechanism of action of IMB-A3, a compound previously shown to exhibit anti-EV-A71 activity.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study characterized the in vitro and in vivo antiviral efficacy of IMB-A3 and investigated its mechanism of action. It included experiments in infected cells and mice muscles, as well as lethal EV-A71 infection models in mice.
analysis_en.methods: The study assessed the effects of IMB-A3 on EV-A71 VP1 protein and viral RNA levels in infected cells and mice muscles. Mechanism studies evaluated the direct interaction between IMB-A3 and the EV-A71 2C protein, its impact on 2C protein activities, and its role in promoting CRBN-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of the 2C protein.
analysis_en.main_results: IMB-A3 treatment reduced EV-A71 VP1 protein and viral RNA levels in infected cells and mice muscles. In vivo, IMB-A3 effectively protected mice from lethal EV-A71 infection. Mechanistically, IMB-A3 facilitated the interaction between 2C and CRBN, promoting ubiquitination and degradation of the N-terminal region of the 2C protein.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that IMB-A3 acts as a molecular glue degrader of the EV-A71 2C protein, providing a mechanistic basis for its antiviral activity. This represents a novel approach to targeting EV-A71 by inducing targeted protein degradation rather than inhibiting enzymatic function.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study identifies IMB-A3 as a promising candidate for the development of targeted antiviral therapies against EV-A71, potentially addressing the current lack of specific treatments. Its mechanism of action suggests broader applicability for designing degraders of viral proteins.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to in vitro and mouse models, which may not fully recapitulate human infection dynamics or safety profiles. While the mechanism is well-characterized, further studies are needed to evaluate efficacy, pharmacokinetics, and safety in humans before clinical translation.

papers.title_zh: IMB-A3 是一种异吲哚酮衍生物,作为分子胶来促进 CRBN 介导的肠道病毒 A71 2C 蛋白的泛素化和降解。
papers.source_body_en: EV-A71 is one of the main culprits causing hand-foot-mouth disease in children. Currently, there are no specific drugs for the prevention and treatment of EV-A71 infection. In our previous studies, a series of 2-aryl-isoindolin-1-one compounds were found to exhibit anti-EV-A71 activity, among which IMB-A3 demonstrated the most potent antiviral activity. Here, we systematically characterized the in vitro and in vivo antiviral efficacy of IMB-A3 and investigated its mechanism of action. The results showed that IMB-A3 treatment decreased the levels of EV-A71 VP1 protein and viral RNA in the infected cells and mice muscles. IMB-A3 could effectively protected mice from lethal EV-A71 infection. Mechanism studies have shown that IMB-A3 interacts directly with the EV-A71 2C protein, but IMB-A3 has no effect on the ATPase and helicase activities of the 2C protein. Interestingly, IMB-A3 acts as a molecular glue to facilitate the interaction between 2C and CRBN, thereby promoting the ubiquitination and degradation of the N-terminal region of the 2C protein and exerting an antiviral effect. These findings indicate that IMB-A3 is a degrader of the EV-A71 2C protein, providing a basis for the future design and development of targeted degraders of the EV-A71 2C protein.

papers.title: Evolutionary and molecular characteristics of high-Shannon entropy codons in VP1 of Coxsackievirus A6
papers.abstract: =12) was uniquely detected in China after 2018. Direct-coupling analysis suggested co-evolution between residue pairs, most notably VP1-137 and VP1-242 (Direct information=0.44), where S137N may form new hydrogen bonds with 243 h, potentially contributing to structural changes that could influence immune evasion. Furthermore, S97N formed hydrogen bonds with D99, thereby altering the BC loop region. A spatiotemporal analysis showed that 283A replaced 283T on a global scale after 2017, while minor variants (e.g. 30D, 97I, 174A) exhibited localized circulation. These findings highlight the predominance of high-entropy codons in VP1 surface loops (BC, DE, EF and HI), suggesting ongoing adaptive selection pressure. Continuous genomic surveillance is imperative for tracking emerging variants (e.g. 283V, 97N) and for informing vaccine design against evolving CVA6 strains.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the evolutionary and molecular features of high-Shannon entropy codons in the VP1 protein of Coxsackievirus A6, focusing on their potential role in immune evasion and structural adaptation. Using direct-coupling analysis and spatiotemporal genomic data, the researchers identified the global replacement of 283A with 283T after 2017 and the localized circulation of minor variants such as 30D, 97I, and 174A. The findings suggest that high-entropy codons in VP1 surface loops are under adaptive selection pressure, which could impact the virus's ability to evade immune responses. The study emphasizes the importance of genomic surveillance to monitor emerging variants and guide vaccine development. However, the analysis is limited by its reliance on existing genomic data without direct functional validation of the observed structural changes. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational nature of the study and the lack of experimental confirmation.

papers.title: Dynamics of neutralizing antibodies against enterovirus D68 in adults during the COVID-19 pandemic.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) causes acute respiratory illnesses and has also implicated in acute flaccid myelitis. Neutralizing antibodies (NtAbs) represent key components of the adaptative immunity. However, the dynamics of EV-D68 NtAbs in adults remain poorly characterized. We evaluated EV-D68 NtAb levels in retail workers in Canada during the COVID-19 pandemic. METHODS: NtAbs were measured in paired serum samples (N=194), from retail workers (≥ 18 years) enrolled in a prospective SARS-CoV-2 cohort at the Centre Hospitalier Universitaire de Québec-Université Laval, in Quebec City. Samples collected 48 weeks apart, between June 2021 to October 2022, were tested by microneutralization assays. RESULTS: EV-D68 NtAb seroprevalence was high (>85%). Over the 48-weeks follow-up, the vast majority of patients (97%) had stable or reduced titers with a statistically significant overall reduction in geometric mean titer (GMT), p<0.001. Furthermore, a small subset of participants 6/194 (3%) showed a marked increase of titers (≥4-fold) with the GMT rising from 21 (10-57) at the first visit to 593 (57-7241) at follow-up visit. CONCLUSIONS: Neutralizing antibody titers declined in most participants over 48 weeks. However, six individuals had significantly increased NtAb titers during the study period, which is consistent with potential ongoing EV-D68 or other enterovirus circulation in Quebec following sequential non-pharmaceutical interventions lift. This is in line with documented EV-D68 resurgence in the United States at the same period. Our work complements pediatric data on EV-D68 immunity and highlights the serological surveillance importance in adults.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) causes acute respiratory illnesses and has been implicated in acute flaccid myelitis, but the dynamics of EV-D68 neutralizing antibodies in adults remain poorly characterized.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We evaluated EV-D68 neutralizing antibody levels in retail workers (≥18 years) in Canada during the COVID-19 pandemic, using paired serum samples (N=194) collected 48 weeks apart between June 2021 and October 2022.
analysis.methods: Neutralizing antibodies were measured in paired serum samples from retail workers enrolled in a prospective SARS-CoV-2 cohort at the Centre Hospitalier Universitaire de Québec-Université Laval, using microneutralization assays.
analysis.main_results: EV-D68 neutralizing antibody seroprevalence was high (>85%), with the vast majority of participants (97%) showing stable or reduced titers over 48 weeks, resulting in a statistically significant overall reduction in geometric mean titer (GMT), p<0.001; however, 6/194 (3%) participants had a marked increase in titers (≥4-fold), with GMT rising from 21 (10-57) to 593 (57-7241).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the decline in neutralizing antibody titers in most participants as evidence of waning immunity, while the increase in a small subset suggested potential ongoing EV-D68 or other enterovirus circulation in Quebec following the lift of non-pharmaceutical interventions, consistent with documented EV-D68 resurgence in the United States during the same period.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This study complements pediatric data on EV-D68 immunity and highlights the importance of serological surveillance in adults to monitor immunity and inform public health responses to enterovirus resurgence.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to retail workers in a single geographic region, and the evidence strength is moderate due to the prospective cohort design but with potential generalizability constraints to other populations or settings.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the dynamics of neutralizing antibodies against enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) in adults during the COVID-19 pandemic. Researchers measured neutralizing antibody levels in paired serum samples from 194 retail workers in Canada, collected 48 weeks apart. The findings revealed high seroprevalence (>85%), with most participants showing stable or reduced titers over time, resulting in a significant overall decline in geometric mean titer (p<0.001). However, a small subset (3%) exhibited a marked increase in titers, suggesting potential ongoing EV-D68 circulation. The study complements pediatric data and underscores the importance of adult serological surveillance for enteroviruses, with moderate evidence strength due to the cohort design but limited generalizability.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 肠道病毒 D68 (EV-D68) 会引起急性呼吸道疾病,并与 急性弛缓性脊髓炎 有关,但成人中 EV-D68 中和抗体的动态仍知之甚少。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们使用 2021 年 6 月至 2022 年 10 月期间相隔 48 周收集的配对血清样本 (N=194) 评估了 COVID-19 大流行期间加拿大零售工人(≥18 岁)的 EV-D68 中和抗体水平。
elements_zh.methods: 使用微量中和测定,在魁北克大学拉瓦尔大学中心医院参加前瞻性 SARS-CoV-2 队列研究 零售工人的配对血清样本中测量中和抗体。
elements_zh.main_results: EV-D68中和抗体血清流行率较高(>85%),绝大多数参与者(97%)在48周内表现出稳定或降低的滴度,导致几何平均滴度(GMT)总体显着降低,p<0.001;然而,6/194 (3%) 参与者的滴度显着增加(≥4 倍),GMT 从 21 (10-57) 上升至 593 (57-7241)。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这项研究补充了有关 EV-D68 免疫力的儿科数据,并强调了成人血清学 监测 对于监测免疫力和告知公共卫生对肠道病毒卷土重来的反应的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于单一地理区域的零售工人,由于前瞻性的 队列研究 设计,证据强度适中,但对其他人群或环境具有潜在的普遍性限制。

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将大多数参与者中和抗体滴度的下降解释为免疫力减弱的证据,而一小部分人的中和抗体滴度的增加表明,在取消非药物干预措施后,魁北克省可能存在持续的 EV-D68 或其他肠道病毒循环,这与同期美国记录的 EV-D68 卷土重来的情况一致。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这项研究补充了有关 EV-D68 免疫力的儿科数据,并强调了成人血清学 监测 对于监测免疫力和告知公共卫生对肠道病毒卷土重来的反应的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于单一地理区域的零售工人,由于前瞻性的 队列研究 设计,证据强度适中,但对其他人群或环境具有潜在的普遍性限制。

papers.title: Boosting Neonatal Immunity: Zymosan-Adjuvanted Intranasal Bivalent Vaccine Shields Against Lethal EV-A71 and EV-D68 Infections 2246328
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Non-polio enteroviruses, particularly EV-D68 and EV-A71, have emerged as major pediatric threats due to their association with acute flaccid myelitis and high mortality. While intranasal vaccines offer a promising route to block viral entry, their effectiveness is limited by poor induction of protective immunity. Zymosan, a yeast cell wall component, has shown its adjuvant potential in multiple vaccine models. This study aims to develop an effective intranasal vaccine incorporating zymosan to protect against EV-D68 and EV-A71 infections. Methods We first prepared an inactivated EV-D68 vaccine to compare immunogenicity across administration routes. Next, we tested monovalent and bivalent intranasal vaccines with zymosan to assess multi-dose and adjuvant effects. Finally, we evaluated vaccine efficacy in a neonatal mouse model. Results Two doses of inactivated EV-D68 with intranasal priming effectively induced mucosal and systemic immunity. A three-dose regimen further strengthened vaccine-specific immunity, with zymosan amplifying responses in both formulations and enhancing serum neutralization. Serum transfer from the zymosan-adjuvanted triple-vaccinated donors afforded significant protection against both viral challenges. Conclusion These findings demonstrated that combining bivalent antigens with zymosan broadened and enhanced the intranasal vaccine efficacy, providing a promising approach for early-life protection against EV-A71 and EV-D68 infections and advancing nasal spray vaccine strategies. Funding Source National Taiwan University Hospital Topic Categories Vaccines and Immunotherapy (VAC)

analysis.study_design_and_population: We evaluated vaccine efficacy in a neonatal mouse model using inactivated EV-D68 vaccines and monovalent and bivalent intranasal vaccines with zymosan.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 非脊髓灰质炎肠道病毒,特别是 EV-D68 和 EV-A71,由于与 急性弛缓性脊髓炎 和高 死亡率 相关,已成为主要的儿科威胁。本研究旨在开发一种包含酵母聚糖的有效鼻内 疫苗,以预防 EV-D68 和 EV-A71 感染。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们使用灭活的 EV-D68 疫苗 以及含有酵母聚糖的单价和二价鼻内 疫苗 评估了 疫苗 在新生小鼠模型中的功效。
elements_zh.methods: 我们首先制备了灭活的 EV-D68 疫苗 以比较不同给药途径的免疫原性。接下来,我们用酵母聚糖测试了单价和二价鼻内 疫苗,以评估多剂量和辅助效果。
elements_zh.main_results: 两剂灭活 EV-D68 鼻内引发有效诱导粘膜和全身免疫。三剂量方案进一步增强了 疫苗 特异性免疫力,酵母聚糖放大了两种配方中的反应并增强了血清中和。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,将二价抗原与酵母聚糖结合扩大并增强了鼻内 疫苗 功效,为生命早期预防 EV-A71 和 EV-D68 感染提供了一种有前景的方法。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现推进了鼻喷雾剂 疫苗 策略,并为生命早期预防 EV-A71 和 EV-D68 感染提供了一种有前途的方法。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据没有报告具体的限制。证据强度很高,因为该研究表明,酵母聚糖佐剂的 疫苗 在新生小鼠模型中具有显着的保护作用。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 简介 非脊髓灰质炎肠道病毒,特别是 EV-D68 和 EV-A71,由于与 急性弛缓性脊髓炎 和高 死亡率 相关,已成为主要的儿科威胁。虽然鼻内 疫苗 提供了一种有希望的阻止病毒进入的途径,但其有效性因保护性免疫诱导不佳而受到限制。酵母聚糖是一种酵母细胞壁成分,已在多个 疫苗 模型中显示出其佐剂潜力。本研究旨在开发一种包含酵母聚糖的有效鼻内 疫苗,以预防 EV-D68 和 EV-A71 感染。方法我们首先制备了灭活的 EV-D68 疫苗 以比较不同给药途径的免疫原性。接下来,我们用酵母聚糖测试了单价和二价鼻内 疫苗,以评估多剂量和辅助效果。最后,我们评估了 疫苗 在新生小鼠模型中的功效。结果 两剂灭活 EV-D68 鼻内引发有效诱导粘膜和全身免疫。三剂量方案进一步增强了 疫苗 特异性免疫力,酵母聚糖放大了两种配方中的反应并增强了血清中和。来自酵母聚糖佐剂的三重疫苗接种供体的血清转移提供了针对这两种病毒挑战的显着保护。结论 这些发现表明,二价抗原与酵母聚糖的组合扩大并增强了鼻内 疫苗 的功效,为生命早期预防 EV-A71 和 EV-D68 感染提供了一种有前景的方法,并推进了鼻喷雾剂 疫苗 策略。资金来源 台大医院 主题类别 疫苗 和免疫治疗 (VAC)

analysis_zh.methods: 我们首先制备了灭活的 EV-D68 疫苗 以比较不同给药途径的免疫原性。接下来,我们用酵母聚糖测试了单价和二价鼻内 疫苗,以评估多剂量和辅助效果。
analysis_zh.main_results: 两剂灭活 EV-D68 鼻内引发有效诱导粘膜和全身免疫。三剂量方案进一步增强了 疫苗 特异性免疫力,酵母聚糖放大了两种配方中的反应并增强了血清中和。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,将二价抗原与酵母聚糖结合扩大并增强了鼻内 疫苗 功效,为生命早期预防 EV-A71 和 EV-D68 感染提供了一种有前景的方法。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现推进了鼻喷雾剂 疫苗 策略,并为生命早期预防 EV-A71 和 EV-D68 感染提供了一种有前途的方法。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据没有报告具体的限制。证据强度很高,因为该研究表明,酵母聚糖佐剂的 疫苗 在新生小鼠模型中具有显着的保护作用。

papers.title: Coxsackievirus B Infections Are Associated With the Risk of Islet Autoimmunity in Children With Strong Genetic Susceptibility to Type 1 Diabetes—Results From the TRIGR Divia Study
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Aims Especially, the coxsackievirus B group of enteroviruses has been linked to the development of islet autoimmunity and type 1 diabetes in genetically susceptible individuals. Our aim was to study the possible associations of 10 different microbial infections with islet autoimmunity in a large international prospective study. Materials and Methods In a nested case‐control study within the TRIGR study, follow‐up serum samples from 240 islet autoantibody‐positive case children and 436 age‐ and country‐matched control children were analysed for IgG class antibodies against 10 different respiratory and gastrointestinal microbes using an enzyme immunoassay, and for neutralising antibodies against all six coxsackievirus B types. The samples were obtained at several time points prior to and at the time of seroconversion for multiple islet autoantibodies. All children had a first‐degree relative with type 1 diabetes, and they carried risk‐associated HLA‐DQ alleles. Results Coxsackievirus B5 was associated with an increased risk of islet autoimmunity (OR 2.22, 95% CI 1.29–3.80, p = 0.004, corrected p = 0.024), which remained after adjustment for HLA, sex, and maternal type 1 diabetes. This association was particularly seen for infections occurring more than 12 months (OR 2.02, 95% CI 1.06–3.84, p = 0.032) and 0–6 months (OR 2.66, 95% CI 1.11–6.35, p = 0.028) before the first detection of multiple islet autoantibodies. After correction for multiple comparisons, none of the other viruses showed an association with islet autoimmunity. Conclusions This study supports previous evidence of the risk association of coxsackievirus B infections. These results support the role of certain virus infections as possible modulating factors in the pathogenesis of type 1 diabetes.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the association between coxsackievirus B infections and islet autoimmunity in children with a genetic predisposition to type 1 diabetes. Using a nested case-control design within the TRIGR study, serum samples from 240 case children and 436 control children were analyzed for antibodies against 10 microbes and all six coxsackievirus B types. The results showed that coxsackievirus B5 was linked to an increased risk of islet autoimmunity, with the association persisting after adjusting for HLA, sex, and maternal diabetes. The risk was particularly notable for infections occurring more than 12 months or within 0–6 months before the first detection of multiple islet autoantibodies. These findings support the role of coxsackievirus B in the pathogenesis of type 1 diabetes and highlight the importance of timing in viral exposure. However, the study's reliance on serum samples and potential confounding factors limit the confidence in the results, though the evidence is considered strong due to the large sample size and statistical adjustments.

papers.title: KREMEN1 residue W94 is essential for receptor binding and infection by a major group of enteroviruses.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT KREMEN1 (KRM1) serves as a cellular receptor for a major group of enteroviruses causing hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD), including CVA2–CVA6, CVA8, CVA10, and CVA12. The viral VP2 residue K140 has recently been identified as completely conserved among these viruses and critical for interaction with KRM1 and viral infection. However, the molecular determinants on the receptor side that govern broad enterovirus recognition remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify KRM1 tryptophan 94 (W94) as an essential residue for KRM1-mediated enterovirus infection. Alanine scanning of 29 KRM1 residues at the CVA10–KRM1 interface revealed that only W94A nearly abolished CVA10 infection. Structural analysis revealed that KRM1 W94 engages in a π-cation interaction with the viral VP2 residue K140, which is critical for receptor binding. Unlike wild-type mice, which succumbed to CVA10 infection, CRISPR-engineered mouse Krm1 W94A mutant mice were fully resistant. Moreover, the W94A mutation conferred universal resistance to all KRM1-dependent enteroviruses (CVA2–CVA6, CVA8, CVA10, and CVA12), both in cell culture and in vivo , indicating that the W94 residue is essential for infection by these viruses. Collectively, these findings establish KRM1 W94 as a critical receptor determinant that pairs with the universally conserved VP2 K140 to enable enterovirus infection. This work provides a structural and mechanistic basis for the broad recognition of KRM1-dependent enteroviruses and offers insights that may guide the future development of broad-spectrum antiviral strategies. IMPORTANCE Hand, foot, and mouth disease affects millions of children worldwide each year; however, no effective antiviral drugs are available. Many causative viruses, including coxsackievirus A10 and A6, rely on the cellular receptor KREMEN1 to enter human cells. However, which parts of the receptor are critical for viral binding and infection have remained unclear. Here, we identified tryptophan 94 (W94) of KREMEN1 as critical for viral infection. Introducing the W94A mutation abolished viral binding and infection. Structural analysis revealed that W94 interacts directly with a completely conserved residue K140 on the viral capsid protein VP2. Notably, mice carrying this mutation were completely resistant to all KREMEN1-dependent viruses. These findings provide a molecular basis for virus-receptor recognition and highlight a promising target for broad-spectrum therapies against hand, foot, and mouth disease.

The viral VP2 residue K140 has recently been identified as completely conserved among these viruses and critical for interaction with KRM1 and viral infection. However, the molecular determinants on the receptor side that govern broad enterovirus recognition remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify KRM1 tryptophan 94 (W94) as an essential residue for KRM1-mediated enterovirus infection. Alanine scanning of 29 KRM1 residues at the CVA10–KRM1 interface revealed that only W94A nearly abolished CVA10 infection. Structural analysis revealed that KRM1 W94 engages in a π-cation interaction with the viral VP2 residue K140, which is critical for receptor binding. Unlike wild-type mice, which succumbed to CVA10 infection, CRISPR-engineered mouse Krm1 W94A mutant mice were fully resistant. Moreover, the W94A mutation conferred universal resistance to all KRM1-dependent enteroviruses (CVA2–CVA6, CVA8, CVA10, and CVA12), both in cell culture and in vivo , indicating that the W94 residue is essential for infection by these viruses. Collectively, these findings establish KRM1 W94 as a critical receptor determinant that pairs with the universally conserved VP2 K140 to enable enterovirus infection. This work provides a structural and mechanistic basis for the broad recognition of KRM1-dependent enteroviruses and offers insights that may guide the future development of broad-spectrum antiviral strategies. IMPORTANCE Hand, foot, and mouth disease affects millions of children worldwide each year; however, no effective antiviral drugs are available. Many causative viruses, including coxsackievirus A10 and A6, rely on the cellular receptor KREMEN1 to enter human cells. However, which parts of the receptor are critical for viral binding and infection have remained unclear. Here, we identified tryptophan 94 (W94) of KREMEN1 as critical for viral infection. Introducing the W94A mutation abolished viral binding and infection. Structural analysis revealed that W94 interacts directly with a completely conserved residue K140 on the viral capsid protein VP2. Notably, mice carrying this mutation were completely resistant to all KREMEN1-dependent viruses. These findings provide a molecular basis for virus-receptor recognition and highlight a promising target for broad-spectrum therapies against hand, foot, and mouth disease.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 KREMEN1 (KRM1) 是导致手足口病 (HFMD) 的主要肠道病毒组的细胞受体,包括 CVA2–CVA6、CVA8、CVA10 和 CVA12。最近发现病毒 VP2 残基 K140 在这些病毒中完全保守,并且对于与 KRM1 和病毒感染的相互作用至关重要。然而,受体侧控制广泛肠道病毒识别的分子决定因素仍不完全清楚。在这里,我们确定 KRM1 色氨酸 94 (W94) 是 KRM1 介导的肠道病毒感染的必需残基。对 CVA10-KRM1 界面上 29 个 KRM1 残基的丙氨酸扫描表明,只有 W94A 几乎消除了 CVA10 感染。结构分析表明,KRM1 W94 与病毒 VP2 残基 K140 发生 π 阳离子相互作用,这对于受体结合至关重要。与死于 CVA10 感染的野生型小鼠不同,CRISPR 工程小鼠 Krm1 W94A 突变小鼠具有完全抵抗力。此外,W94A 突变 在细胞培养物和体内均对所有 KRM1 依赖性肠道病毒(CVA2-CVA6、CVA8、CVA10 和 CVA12)具有普遍抗性,表明 W94 残基对于这些病毒的感染至关重要。总的来说,这些发现确定 KRM1 W94 是一个关键的受体决定簇,它与普遍保守的 VP2 K140 配对以实现肠道病毒感染。这项工作为广泛认识 KRM1 依赖性肠道病毒提供了结构和机制基础,并提供了可能指导广谱 抗病毒药物 策略未来发展的见解。重要性 手足口病每年影响全世界数百万儿童;然而,目前尚无有效的 抗病毒药物 药物。许多致病病毒,包括柯萨奇病毒 A10 和 A6,依赖细胞受体 KREMEN1 进入人体细胞。然而,受体的哪些部分对于病毒结合和感染至关重要仍不清楚。在这里,我们确定 KREMEN1 的色氨酸 94 (W94) 对于病毒感染至关重要。W94A 突变 的推出消除了病毒结合和感染。结构分析表明,W94 直接与病毒衣壳蛋白 VP2 上完全保守的残基 K140 相互作用。值得注意的是,携带这种 突变 的小鼠对所有 KREMEN1 依赖性病毒完全具有抵抗力。这些发现为病毒受体识别提供了分子基础,并强调了针对手足口病的广谱疗法的一个有希望的目标。

papers.title: Onychomadesis: nail shedding as a delayed manifestation of hand, foot, and mouth disease
papers.abstract: Key pointsWhat is known -Onychomadesis involves the complete shedding of a nail from the proximal nail bed due to the cessation of nail plate production.-Coxsackievirus A6 and A10 have emerged as major agents of atypical hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) and post-infection onychomadesis.-The nail matrix recovers spontaneously within three to six months.Reassuring parents avoids unnecessary interventions during the recovery period.What is added -Nail diseases are rare in children but should alert healthcare professionals for proper evaluation and management.-Viral replication in the nail matrix can cause temporary nail growth arrest and nail shedding.-Coxsackievirus A10 can interfere with the Wnt/-catenin signaling involved in nail growth and disrupt cell proliferation and nail stem cell differentiation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the rare manifestation of onychomadesis (nail shedding) as a delayed complication of hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD), focusing on the role of coxsackievirus A6 and A10 in disrupting nail matrix function and growth.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a review article that synthesizes current knowledge on onychomadesis, its association with HFMD, and the viral mechanisms involved in nail matrix disruption.
analysis.methods: The methods involve a literature review summarizing the pathophysiology of onychomadesis, viral replication in the nail matrix, and the interference with Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathways.
analysis.main_results: The findings confirm that coxsackievirus A10 can disrupt nail growth by interfering with Wnt/β-catenin signaling, leading to temporary nail growth arrest and shedding, with spontaneous recovery within three to six months.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret onychomadesis as a rare but significant complication of HFMD, with novel insights into the viral interference of nail stem cell differentiation and proliferation pathways.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the importance of recognizing onychomadesis as a post-infection complication to avoid unnecessary interventions and reassure parents during the recovery period.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate, as the study is a review article without primary data, but it provides a comprehensive synthesis of existing literature on the topic.

analysis.summary_en: This review article explores onychomadesis, a rare complication of hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD), focusing on the role of coxsackievirus A6 and A10 in disrupting nail matrix function. The study highlights that viral replication in the nail matrix can cause temporary nail growth arrest and shedding, with spontaneous recovery within three to six months. The authors provide novel insights into how coxsackievirus A10 interferes with Wnt/β-catenin signaling, disrupting cell proliferation and nail stem cell differentiation. The findings emphasize the importance of recognizing onychomadesis as a post-infection manifestation to avoid unnecessary interventions and reassure parents. While the evidence is moderate due to the review nature of the study, it offers valuable guidance for healthcare professionals in managing this condition.

news.content: Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease (HFMD) is caused primarily by two types of viruses: Coxsackievirus A6 & A16 and Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) . This disease primarily affects young children and can sometimes lead to severe complications. Symptoms typically appear 2–3 days after incubation, starting with fever. HFMD is most common in children aged 6 months to 5 years. However, both children and caregivers can take preventive measures to reduce the risk of infection. Symptoms of HFMD The initial symptoms of HFMD include high fever, decreased appetite, and excessive drooling. Upon physical examination, ulcers can be found inside the cheeks and on the soft palate. Red spots or fluid-filled blisters may appear on the palms, soles of the feet, buttocks, genitals, arms, and legs. These symptoms generally improve within 2–3 days. Most children over the age of 5 develop immunity to the virus and are less likely to contract the disease. Although rare, adults who have never been infected and have not developed immunity may also contract HFMD, as can older children who lack prior exposure to the virus. Transmission of HFMD HFMD spreads through direct contact with nasal secretions, saliva, or feces of an infected person. The virus is especially concentrated in stool, making it highly contagious. Infected children may also transmit the virus through contact with fluid from blisters. The virus can persist in the body for weeks or even months after recovery, meaning that individuals can continue to spread the infection even after symptoms subside. Indirect transmission is also possible through contaminated objects. For example, if an infected child touches toys, other children who play with the same toys can contract the virus. Additionally, HFMD can spread through contaminated food or water, making young children particularly vulnerable. High-Risk Environments Childcare facilities, especially nurseries where caregivers frequently change diapers, pose a high risk for HFMD transmission. If proper hygiene practices are not followed, the virus can easily spread through contaminated hands or surfaces. Play areas, such as ball pits, are also potential hotspots due to inadequate cleaning. Most children recover from HFMD without complications. However, infections caused by Enterovirus A71 can lead to severe complications. Complications of HFMD Severe complications from HFMD include brainstem encephalitis, meningitis, heart failure, and acute paralysis , all of which can be life-threatening. Warning signs of serious complications include lethargy, muscle weakness, seizures, tremors, difficulty walking, rapid breathing, and vomiting. If any of these symptoms appear, immediate medical attention is required. No Specific Treatment Available Currently, no antiviral medication specifically targets HFMD. Treatment focuses on managing symptoms. Fever-reducing medications can be used to control fever. If a child has difficulty eating, intravenous fluids may be administered. Soft, easily digestible, and cold foods that do not irritate the mouth are recommended, along with adequate hydration to support recovery. HFMD Prevention Caregivers can help prevent HFMD by avoiding contact with contaminated surfaces and maintaining proper hygiene. Since this virus is resistant to alcohol-based hand sanitizers, proper handwashing with soap and water is crucial. Key preventive measures include: Frequent Handwashing: Wash hands with soap and water before and after meals, after using the restroom, and after changing diapers. Avoiding Shared Items: Children should not share utensils, bottles, or other personal items, particularly in schools or daycare settings. Cleaning Toys and Surfaces: Parents should regularly clean toys and play areas using soap and water, thoroughly drying them before use. Detergents can also be used for disinfection. Keeping Sick Children at Home: If a child is unwell, they should stay home to prevent spreading the virus to others. HFMD Vaccination A vaccine is available to protect against HFMD caused by Enterovirus A71 . Children aged 6 months to under 6 years can receive two doses, administered one month apart. This vaccine is safe and helps reduce the risk of severe complications from HFMD. Further Reading: HFMD: A Common Childhood Illness During the Rainy Season

news.content_original: Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease (HFMD) is caused primarily by two types of viruses: Coxsackievirus A6 & A16 and Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) . This disease primarily affects young children and can sometimes lead to severe complications. Symptoms typically appear 2–3 days after incubation, starting with fever. HFMD is most common in children aged 6 months to 5 years. However, both children and caregivers can take preventive measures to reduce the risk of infection. Symptoms of HFMD The initial symptoms of HFMD include high fever, decreased appetite, and excessive drooling. Upon physical examination, ulcers can be found inside the cheeks and on the soft palate. Red spots or fluid-filled blisters may appear on the palms, soles of the feet, buttocks, genitals, arms, and legs. These symptoms generally improve within 2–3 days. Most children over the age of 5 develop immunity to the virus and are less likely to contract the disease. Although rare, adults who have never been infected and have not developed immunity may also contract HFMD, as can older children who lack prior exposure to the virus. Transmission of HFMD HFMD spreads through direct contact with nasal secretions, saliva, or feces of an infected person. The virus is especially concentrated in stool, making it highly contagious. Infected children may also transmit the virus through contact with fluid from blisters. The virus can persist in the body for weeks or even months after recovery, meaning that individuals can continue to spread the infection even after symptoms subside. Indirect transmission is also possible through contaminated objects. For example, if an infected child touches toys, other children who play with the same toys can contract the virus. Additionally, HFMD can spread through contaminated food or water, making young children particularly vulnerable. High-Risk Environments Childcare facilities, especially nurseries where caregivers frequently change diapers, pose a high risk for HFMD transmission. If proper hygiene practices are not followed, the virus can easily spread through contaminated hands or surfaces. Play areas, such as ball pits, are also potential hotspots due to inadequate cleaning. Most children recover from HFMD without complications. However, infections caused by Enterovirus A71 can lead to severe complications. Complications of HFMD Severe complications from HFMD include brainstem encephalitis, meningitis, heart failure, and acute paralysis , all of which can be life-threatening. Warning signs of serious complications include lethargy, muscle weakness, seizures, tremors, difficulty walking, rapid breathing, and vomiting. If any of these symptoms appear, immediate medical attention is required. No Specific Treatment Available Currently, no antiviral medication specifically targets HFMD. Treatment focuses on managing symptoms. Fever-reducing medications can be used to control fever. If a child has difficulty eating, intravenous fluids may be administered. Soft, easily digestible, and cold foods that do not irritate the mouth are recommended, along with adequate hydration to support recovery. HFMD Prevention Caregivers can help prevent HFMD by avoiding contact with contaminated surfaces and maintaining proper hygiene. Since this virus is resistant to alcohol-based hand sanitizers, proper handwashing with soap and water is crucial. Key preventive measures include: Frequent Handwashing: Wash hands with soap and water before and after meals, after using the restroom, and after changing diapers. Avoiding Shared Items: Children should not share utensils, bottles, or other personal items, particularly in schools or daycare settings. Cleaning Toys and Surfaces: Parents should regularly clean toys and play areas using soap and water, thoroughly drying them before use. Detergents can also be used for disinfection. Keeping Sick Children at Home: If a child is unwell, they should stay home to prevent spreading the virus to others. HFMD Vaccination A vaccine is available to protect against HFMD caused by Enterovirus A71 . Children aged 6 months to under 6 years can receive two doses, administered one month apart. This vaccine is safe and helps reduce the risk of severe complications from HFMD. Further Reading: HFMD: A Common Childhood Illness During the Rainy Season

Conditions Sudden Arm or Leg Weakness in a Child Is an Emergency, and Late Summer Is When It Has Appeared Before Published Jul 30, 2026 12:00 PM EDT By Elena Vega ORLANDO SIERRA | AFP via Getty Images Share on Twitter Share on Facebook Share on Pocket What Parents Should Recognize The scenario worth knowing is specific: a child who had a cold or a fever in the past week or two suddenly cannot lift an arm, or a leg gives out. Acute flaccid myelitis is a rare neurologic condition that causes sudden weakness in one or more limbs, with damage to the gray matter of the spinal cord. It predominantly affects previously healthy children, and it can progress quickly, in some cases to breathing difficulty requiring intensive care. The weakness is the signal. It is flaccid, meaning the limb is limp rather than stiff, and it comes on over hours to days rather than gradually. It frequently follows a respiratory illness or fever by a few days to a couple of weeks. CDC guidance to clinicians has been consistent across surveillance reports: suspect AFM "in any child with acute flaccid limb weakness," particularly after a recent febrile or respiratory illness. Escalation signs matter more than the initial weakness. Neck weakness or difficulty holding the head up, facial droop, drooping eyelids, difficulty swallowing, slurred speech, or any change in breathing all indicate the problem may be affecting muscles needed to protect the airway. Those warrant emergency care immediately rather than a call to the pediatrician's office. What the New Surveillance Report Found The report published this month is reassuring on frequency, which is worth stating clearly before anything else. Between 2020 and 2025, the CDC recorded between 17 and 48 AFM cases nationally per year. For comparison, the peak years of 2014, 2016 and 2018 produced 120 to 238 cases annually. The more interesting finding is that cases stayed low even when the virus most associated with AFM did not. Enterovirus D68, or EV-D68, drove those earlier peaks, and the report notes increases in EV-D68-associated respiratory illness in 2022, 2024, and 2025 without a corresponding rise in AFM. Why that link appears to have weakened is not established. It may reflect changes in circulating viral strains, population immunity, or factors not yet identified. The honest position is that nobody knows, and nobody can currently predict when or whether cases will rise again. For a parent, the practical meaning is proportion. AFM is genuinely rare, and the overwhelming majority of children who get a summer respiratory virus will not develop it. Nothing in this report suggests families should worry more this year than last. Why Late Summer Matters The seasonality is real, and it comes from the virus rather than from anything about the season itself. In the peak years, AFM cases clustered in late summer and early fall. That timing tracks enterovirus circulation, which rises as children return to school and shed viruses in close quarters. Enteroviruses are a large family, most of which cause nothing worse than a summer cold, hand-foot-and-mouth disease, or a few days of fever. So the window from roughly August through October is when clinicians historically have been most alert. That is useful context for a parent trying to judge whether a symptom deserves urgency, and it is also a reason not to over-read it, since low case counts have held through recent seasons regardless of month. Cases have been reported in 49 states and the District of Columbia over the surveillance period, so this is not a regional concern. There is no vaccine for EV-D68 and no specific antiviral treatment for AFM. Care is supportive, focused on protecting breathing and swallowing and on rehabilitation afterward. Historical data indicate that roughly half of patients required intensive care and a smaller share required mechanical ventilation. The Polio Question in the Report The finding likely to matter most to public health is one a parent might otherwise skip, and it has a simple household action attached. AFM is, in the report's words, clinically and radiologically indistinguishable from the paralysis caused by poliovirus. A doctor looking at a child with sudden limb weakness and an MRI showing spinal cord lesions cannot tell from those alone which one they are dealing with. That makes laboratory testing the only way to distinguish them, and the report found a gap. Approximately half of AFM patients had stool specimens tested for poliovirus. The recommendation is that stool specimens should be collected and tested from all patients suspected of having AFM. The reason this is not theoretical: one polio case was identified in New York in 2022. The report also found that between 75 and 100 percent of AFM patients had received three or more polio vaccine doses, and its stated implication is that "remaining current with polio vaccinations can reduce the risk for poliovirus infection." For families, that is the concrete takeaway. The routine childhood polio series is protection against the one preventable cause of sudden paralysis. When to Go to the Emergency Department The decision rule here is simpler than most, because the threshold for acting is low. Go to an emergency department, or call 911, for sudden weakness in an arm or leg in a child, particularly following a recent illness. Do not wait for a next-day appointment, and do not wait to see whether it improves. Rapid evaluation matters because the condition can progress and because supportive care is most effective when started early. Call 911 rather than driving for any difficulty breathing, difficulty swallowing or managing saliva, slurred speech, or a child who cannot hold up their head. At the hospital, it is reasonable to ask whether AFM is being considered, whether an MRI of the spine is planned, and whether stool and respiratory specimens are being collected. Those questions are appropriate rather than pushy, and given the testing gap the report identified, the stool specimen question is fair. Confirm your child's polio vaccinations are current at the next well visit. Complaining of tired legs after a long day is not this. Waking up unable to lift an arm is. The confirmed findings are 17 to 48 annual AFM cases since 2020, well below the peak years, with no rise despite increased EV-D68 activity. Those most affected are previously healthy children, historically in late summer and early fall. Reasonable actions include emergency evaluation for sudden limb weakness and keeping polio vaccination current. The central uncertainty is why the link to EV-D68 weakened and whether cases will peak again. The next expected development is CDC's next annual surveillance update. Here Is What That Means and How It Happened U.S. Measles Cases Hit 35-Year High in 2026, Surpassing 2,295 With Five Months Left Frequently Asked Questions What is acute flaccid myelitis? A rare neurologic condition causing sudden limp weakness in one or more limbs, with spinal cord damage. It mainly affects previously healthy children. How common is it? Rare. CDC recorded 17 to 48 cases per year nationally from 2020 through 2025, compared with 120 to 238 in the peak years of 2014, 2016, and 2018. Is it rising this year? No. The report found cases stayed low even as EV-D68 respiratory illness increased in 2022, 2024 and 2025. Why that link weakened is unknown. What symptoms mean go to the emergency room? Sudden weakness in an arm or leg, especially after a recent illness. Call 911 for breathing or swallowing difficulty, slurred speech or neck weakness. Is there a treatment? No specific antiviral exists. Care is supportive, focused on breathing and swallowing, followed by rehabilitation. What does polio vaccination have to do with it? AFM is indistinguishable from polio paralysis without lab testing. Staying current on polio vaccination protects against the one preventable cause. Will my child get this from a summer cold? Almost certainly not. Enteroviruses are extremely common and AFM is very rare. The point is recognition, not expectation. Conditions Sudden Arm or Leg Weakness in a Child Is an Emergency, and Late Summer Is When It Has Appeared Before Published Jul 30, 2026 12:00 PM EDT By Elena Vega ORLANDO SIERRA | AFP via Getty Images Share on Twitter Share on Facebook Share on Pocket What Parents Should Recognize The scenario worth knowing is specific: a child who had a cold or a fever in the past week or two suddenly cannot lift an arm, or a leg gives out. Acute flaccid myelitis is a rare neurologic condition that causes sudden weakness in one or more limbs, with damage to the gray matter of the spinal cord. It predominantly affects previously healthy children, and it can progress quickly, in some cases to breathing difficulty requiring intensive care. The weakness is the signal. It is flaccid, meaning the limb is limp rather than stiff, and it comes on over hours to days rather than gradually. It frequently follows a respiratory illness or fever by a few days to a couple of weeks. CDC guidance to clinicians has been consistent across surveillance reports: suspect AFM "in any child with acute flaccid limb weakness," particularly after a recent febrile or respiratory illness. Escalation signs matter more than the initial weakness. Neck weakness or difficulty holding the head up, facial droop, drooping eyelids, difficulty swallowing, slurred speech, or any change in breathing all indicate the problem may be affecting muscles needed to protect the airway. Those warrant emergency care immediately rather than a call to the pediatrician's office. What the New Surveillance Report Found The report published this month is reassuring on frequency, which is worth stating clearly before anything else. Between 2020 and 2025, the CDC recorded between 17 and 48 AFM cases nationally per year. For comparison, the peak years of 2014, 2016 and 2018 produced 120 to 238 cases annually. The more interesting finding is that cases stayed low even when the virus most associated with AFM did not. Enterovirus D68, or EV-D68, drove those earlier peaks, and the report notes increases in EV-D68-associated respiratory illness in 2022, 2024, and 2025 without a corresponding rise in AFM. Why that link appears to have weakened is not established. It may reflect changes in circulating viral strains, population immunity, or factors not yet identified. The honest position is that nobody knows, and nobody can currently predict when or whether cases will rise again. For a parent, the practical meaning is proportion. AFM is genuinely rare, and the overwhelming majority of children who get a summer respiratory virus will not develop it. Nothing in this report suggests families should worry more this year than last. Why Late Summer Matters The seasonality is real, and it comes from the virus rather than from anything about the season itself. In the peak years, AFM cases clustered in late summer and early fall. That timing tracks enterovirus circulation, which rises as children return to school and shed viruses in close quarters. Enteroviruses are a large family, most of which cause nothing worse than a summer cold, hand-foot-and-mouth disease, or a few days of fever. So the window from roughly August through October is when clinicians historically have been most alert. That is useful context for a parent trying to judge whether a symptom deserves urgency, and it is also a reason not to over-read it, since low case counts have held through recent seasons regardless of month. Cases have been reported in 49 states and the District of Columbia over the surveillance period, so this is not a regional concern. There is no vaccine for EV-D68 and no specific antiviral treatment for AFM. Care is supportive, focused on protecting breathing and swallowing and on rehabilitation afterward. Historical data indicate that roughly half of patients required intensive care and a smaller share required mechanical ventilation. The Polio Question in the Report The finding likely to matter most to public health is one a parent might otherwise skip, and it has a simple household action attached. AFM is, in the report's words, clinically and radiologically indistinguishable from the paralysis caused by poliovirus. A doctor looking at a child with sudden limb weakness and an MRI showing spinal cord lesions cannot tell from those alone which one they are dealing with. That makes laboratory testing the only way to distinguish them, and the report found a gap. Approximately half of AFM patients had stool specimens tested for poliovirus. The recommendation is that stool specimens should be collected and tested from all patients suspected of having AFM. The reason this is not theoretical: one polio case was identified in New York in 2022. The report also found that between 75 and 100 percent of AFM patients had received three or more polio vaccine doses, and its stated implication is that "remaining current with polio vaccinations can reduce the risk for poliovirus infection." For families, that is the concrete takeaway. The routine childhood polio series is protection against the one preventable cause of sudden paralysis. When to Go to the Emergency Department The decision rule here is simpler than most, because the threshold for acting is low. Go to an emergency department, or call 911, for sudden weakness in an arm or leg in a child, particularly following a recent illness. Do not wait for a next-day appointment, and do not wait to see whether it improves. Rapid evaluation matters because the condition can progress and because supportive care is most effective when started early. Call 911 rather than driving for any difficulty breathing, difficulty swallowing or managing saliva, slurred speech, or a child who cannot hold up their head. At the hospital, it is reasonable to ask whether AFM is being considered, whether an MRI of the spine is planned, and whether stool and respiratory specimens are being collected. Those questions are appropriate rather than pushy, and given the testing gap the report identified, the stool specimen question is fair. Confirm your child's polio vaccinations are current at the next well visit. Complaining of tired legs after a long day is not this. Waking up unable to lift an arm is. The confirmed findings are 17 to 48 annual AFM cases since 2020, well below the peak years, with no rise despite increased EV-D68 activity. Those most affected are previously healthy children, historically in late summer and early fall. Reasonable actions include emergency evaluation for sudden limb weakness and keeping polio vaccination current. The central uncertainty is why the link to EV-D68 weakened and whether cases will peak again. The next expected development is CDC's next annual surveillance update. A rare neurologic condition causing sudden limp weakness in one or more limbs, with spinal cord damage. It mainly affects previously healthy children. How common is it? Rare. CDC recorded 17 to 48 cases per year nationally from 2020 through 2025, compared with 120 to 238 in the peak years of 2014, 2016, and 2018. Is it rising this year? No. The report found cases stayed low even as EV-D68 respiratory illness increased in 2022, 2024 and 2025. Why that link weakened is unknown. What symptoms mean go to the emergency room? Sudden weakness in an arm or leg, especially after a recent illness. Call 911 for breathing or swallowing difficulty, slurred speech or neck weakness. Is there a treatment? No specific antiviral exists. Care is supportive, focused on breathing and swallowing, followed by rehabilitation. What does polio vaccination have to do with it? AFM is indistinguishable from polio paralysis without lab testing. Staying current on polio vaccination protects against the one preventable cause. Will my child get this from a summer cold? Almost certainly not. Enteroviruses are extremely common and AFM is very rare. The point is recognition, not expectation. analysis.brief_en: A rare but serious neurologic condition, acute flaccid myelitis (AFM), causes sudden limb weakness in children, typically following a respiratory illness. CDC urges parents and clinicians to recognize this as a medical emergency, especially when accompanied by symptoms like facial droop or breathing difficulties. While cases have been reported across the U.S., recent data shows lower frequency compared to previous peaks. news.content_title: Probable Coxsackievirus Infection in an Immunocompetent Adult With Genital and Oral Ulcerations Mimicking Herpes Simplex Virus Infection and Behçet’s Disease
news.content: Abstract Disseminated viral infections in immunocompetent adults are uncommon and may mimic autoimmune or bacterial conditions, including Behçet’s disease and disseminated herpes simplex virus (HSV) infection. We report a case of a 33-year-old immunocompetent woman who developed severe, painful vulvar ulcerations, oral ulcers, and a painful maculopapular rash involving both lower extremities that evolved into pustules. She was afebrile and hemodynamically stable but demonstrated a marked systemic inflammatory response, including leukocytosis (white blood cell count: 21.3×109/L; 85% neutrophils) and elevated inflammatory markers (erythrocyte sedimentation rate: 42 mm/h; C-reactive protein: 15.4 mg/dL). Extensive infectious and autoimmune evaluation was unrevealing, and imaging showed no drainable pelvic fluid collection. She received empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics and was transitioned to valacyclovir for suspected disseminated HSV infection; leukocytosis improved rapidly with persistently sterile cultures. Subsequent serologic testing demonstrated elevated Coxsackievirus A and B titers (≥1:100), supporting an enteroviral etiology in the appropriate clinical context; however, the limitations of serologic testing preclude definitive confirmation of acute infection in the absence of paired titers or lesion-based polymerase chain reaction testing. She was transferred to a tertiary center for dermatologic evaluation due to the absence of local specialty services, where skin biopsy demonstrated nonspecific inflammatory changes with negative direct immunofluorescence, arguing against immune complex-mediated vasculitis. This case highlights a rare adult presentation of Coxsackievirus infection with prominent genital and oral ulcerations mimicking HSV and Behçet’s disease, underscoring the importance of considering viral etiologies in sterile inflammatory mucocutaneous eruptions to avoid unnecessary antimicrobial exposure. Introduction Enteroviruses, including Coxsackieviruses, classically cause self-limited febrile illness and hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) in children. However, adult infections are increasingly recognized and may present with more severe and atypical mucocutaneous manifestations than traditionally described, including disseminated involvement characterized by widespread cutaneous and mucosal disease extending beyond the classic palmoplantar distribution [1-3]. Outbreaks associated with Coxsackievirus A6 have demonstrated an expanded clinical spectrum, including vesiculobullous eruptions and widespread cutaneous involvement [1,2,4]. Early recognition of these atypical presentations is important to support antimicrobial stewardship by avoiding unnecessary broad-spectrum antibiotic and antiviral exposure. Acute painful oral and genital ulcerations accompanied by systemic inflammation in an immunocompetent host can closely resemble disseminated herpes simplex virus (HSV) infection, sexually transmitted infections, drug eruptions, or inflammatory disorders, such as Behçet's disease, a chronic systemic vasculitis characterized by recurrent oral and genital ulcerations with potential ocular, vascular, and neurologic involvement [5,6]. This diagnostic overlap may prompt extensive testing and empiric antimicrobial therapy before viral etiologies are considered. We describe an immunocompetent adult presenting with painful oral and vulvar ulcerations and a pustular lower-extremity eruption initially concerning for disseminated HSV infection and Behçet's disease, later supported by elevated Coxsackievirus serologies. Although several reports have documented atypical adult Coxsackievirus presentations, including widespread vesiculobullous eruptions, purpuric lesions, and eczema coxsackium, reports of adult enteroviral infection presenting with severe genital and oral ulcerations, pustular lower-extremity lesions, and a clinical picture closely resembling both disseminated herpes simplex virus infection and Behçet's disease have not been previously described [3]. Case Presentation A 33-year-old immunocompetent woman with no significant past medical history presented with severe vulvar pain and mucocutaneous lesions. Symptoms began approximately one week prior with vulvar burning that progressed to severe, painful labial ulcerations. Over the subsequent 48 h, she developed painful oral mucosal ulcerations and a maculopapular rash involving both lower extremities that evolved into tender pustules. The eruption spared the trunk, palms, and soles. She reported malaise and chills prior to admission but was uncertain about documented fever. She denied recent sexual activity, prior sexually transmitted infections, autoimmune disease, or similar dermatologic episodes. Recent travel included a trip to Toronto, though symptoms preceded travel. She was not immunocompromised and was not receiving immunosuppressive therapy. On presentation, she was afebrile and hemodynamically stable. Physical examination revealed irregular vulvar and perineal ulcerations with whitish discoloration and no purulent drainage, along with multiple shallow, round-to-oval oral ulcers with erythematous borders involving the buccal mucosa, ranging from approximately 3 to 5 mm in diameter. Autoimmune evaluation, including antinuclear antibody and HLA-B51 testing, was unrevealing (Table 2). Over the subsequent three days, leukocytosis improved from 21.3 to 8.7×109/L with continued clinical stability and persistently negative cultures (Table 3). Empiric antibacterial therapy was administered for approximately three days and discontinued following improvement in leukocytosis and persistently sterile cultures. Supportive care included topical analgesics and local wound care for the mucocutaneous lesions. Because dermatology services were unavailable locally, the patient was transferred to a tertiary care center for further evaluation and consideration of a biopsy. Subsequent serologic testing demonstrated elevated Coxsackievirus A (A7-A24) and B (B1-B6) titers (≥1:100), suggesting recent enteroviral exposure in the appropriate clinical context. Following the transfer, dermatologic evaluation was performed. A skin biopsy obtained from a representative lower-extremity lesion demonstrated nonspecific inflammatory changes without evidence of leukocytoclastic vasculitis or viral cytopathic effect. Frozen section confirmed adequate tissue sampling for direct immunofluorescence, which was negative for all immunoreactants, including IgA, IgG, IgM, C3, albumin, and fibrinogen, arguing against immune complex-mediated vasculitis. During that hospitalization, the patient also developed transient bilateral ankle arthralgia with mild swelling, consistent with an acute inflammatory process. No erosive changes or features suggestive of chronic inflammatory arthritis were identified. The patient was subsequently contacted for follow-up and provided the final pathological results, which confirmed these findings. At follow-up, the vulvar and oral ulcerations had resolved, and the lower-extremity eruption had faded without scarring. No recurrence of symptoms was reported. Focal interface changes are identified. Within the superficial dermis, there is a perivascular inflammatory infiltrate composed predominantly of lymphocytes, with occasional neutrophils. There is a perifollicular inflammatory infiltrate with occasional neutrophils. Focally, a superficial blood vessel with thrombus formation is identified. Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS), Grocott’s methenamine silver (GMS), and Fite-Faraco stains, with appropriate controls, are negative for microorganisms. Multiple deeper sections were examined. Reported adult manifestations include vesiculobullous eruptions, eczema coxsackium, and widespread cutaneous disease, reflecting an expanded clinical spectrum beyond classic pediatric presentations. In this case, the presence of painful oral and genital ulcerations with systemic inflammation appropriately raised concern for disseminated HSV infection and inflammatory disorders such as Behçet's disease. Disseminated HSV remains an important diagnostic consideration given its potential severity and need for prompt antiviral therapy [8]. Behçet's disease is characterized by recurrent oral and genital ulcerations with possible multisystem involvement; however, the absence of prior episodes, lack of ocular or neurologic findings, and negative autoimmune evaluation made a primary inflammatory disorder less likely in this patient [9,10]. Additionally, dermatopathological evaluation at the tertiary center demonstrated nonspecific inflammatory changes and negative direct immunofluorescence, arguing against immune complex-mediated vasculitis and further reducing concern for an underlying autoimmune vasculitis. The clinical distinction among these entities can be further clarified by their characteristic features. Disseminated HSV typically presents with grouped vesicles on an erythematous base that evolve into shallow ulcerations, often with positive viral PCR or culture and characteristic multinucleated giant cells on biopsy. Behçet's disease is defined by recurrent episodes of oral and genital ulcerations, often accompanied by ocular inflammation, pathergy, or neurologic involvement, with biopsy typically showing neutrophilic vasculitis. In contrast, the present case demonstrated a single episode of oral and genital ulcerations with a pustular lower-extremity eruption, negative HSV PCR, negative autoimmune markers, no prior episodes, and biopsy findings showing nonspecific perivascular inflammation without vasculitis or viral cytopathic effect, a pattern more consistent with a self-limited viral process than with either HSV or Behçet's disease. Beyond HSV and Behçet's disease, several other entities warrant consideration in the differential diagnosis of acute oral and genital ulcerations. Lipschütz ulcer is characterized by the sudden onset of painful, necrotic vulvar ulcerations in young women, often preceded by a flu-like prodrome, and has been linked to Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, and Mycoplasma species. Like the present case, Lipschütz ulcers are a diagnosis of exclusion, demonstrate nonspecific histopathology, and resolve spontaneously within two to four weeks. However, Lipschütz ulcers typically present with deep necrotic ulcerations rather than the pustular lower-extremity eruption observed in our patient and are not typically associated with enteroviral infection. Mycoplasma pneumoniae-induced rash and mucositis (MIRM) is another important consideration, characterized by prominent oral, ocular, and urogenital mucositis with sparse cutaneous involvement, typically following respiratory symptoms. The absence of respiratory symptoms, negative findings for Mycoplasma, and the prominent pustular cutaneous eruption in our patient argued against MIRM. Erythema multiforme, which may present with oral and genital mucosal erosions and targetoid cutaneous lesions, was also considered; however, the absence of classic target lesions and the pustular rather than vesiculobullous morphology of the skin eruption made this diagnosis less likely. The clinical overlap among these entities underscores the diagnostic challenge posed by acute mucocutaneous ulcerations and the importance of a systematic approach to exclude infectious, inflammatory, and reactive etiologies [3,7]. Although Coxsackievirus serologic testing has limitations, including cross-reactivity and the inability to definitively confirm acute infection without paired titers or lesion-based polymerase chain reaction, elevated titers in the setting of a compatible clinical syndrome and exclusion of alternative etiologies support an enteroviral cause. Paired acute and convalescent titers were not obtained in this case, which would have strengthened the serologic evidence by demonstrating a fourfold rise in antibody levels. Additionally, lesion-based PCR was not performed for either enterovirus or HSV, as dermatology services and specialized virologic testing were unavailable at the initial facility; the patient required transfer to a tertiary center for biopsy alone. Notably, HSV-1 and HSV-2 PCR testing was performed on serum rather than from lesion swabs, which may reduce diagnostic sensitivity for mucocutaneous HSV infection, as lesion-based PCR is the preferred method for detecting active cutaneous or genital herpes simplex virus infection. The absence of definitive virologic confirmation, either through lesion PCR or paired serologies, represents the principal diagnostic limitation of this report. When available, lesion polymerase chain reaction testing may further improve diagnostic certainty. This case underscores the importance of considering viral etiologies in immunocompetent adults presenting with sterile inflammatory mucocutaneous eruptions and systemic inflammatory responses. Early recognition of atypical enteroviral infections may facilitate timely antimicrobial de-escalation, reduce unnecessary broad-spectrum antibiotic exposure, and mitigate medication-related adverse effects, supporting antimicrobial stewardship efforts [11]. Conclusions Coxsackievirus infection, classically associated with pediatric hand-foot-and-mouth disease, can present atypically in immunocompetent adults with severe mucocutaneous involvement and a marked systemic inflammatory response. In this case, prominent genital and oral ulcerations with leukocytosis and elevated inflammatory markers closely mimicked disseminated HSV infection and inflammatory disorders such as Behçet's disease, creating substantial diagnostic uncertainty. The absence of positive bacterial cultures, negative herpes simplex virus testing, unremarkable autoimmune evaluation, and nondiagnostic biopsy findings, combined with elevated Coxsackievirus serologic titers in a compatible clinical context, supported but did not definitively confirm an enteroviral etiology. Recognition of this atypical presentation is important to avoid unnecessary antimicrobial exposure, reduce invasive diagnostic interventions, and support appropriate supportive care. Subsequent serologic testing showed elevated Coxsackievirus A and B titers, supporting a probable enteroviral etiology, though definitive confirmation was limited by testing methodology. This rare case highlights the diagnostic challenges of atypical adult Coxsackievirus presentations, which can mimic more common conditions, and underscores the importance of considering viral etiologies to avoid unnecessary antimicrobial exposure.

elements_en.time: Published on 2026-08-01. Event date: approximately one week prior to admission (patient presented with symptoms beginning about a week before admission).
elements_en.location_and_population: Country not specified. Patient: 33-year-old immunocompetent woman with no significant past medical history, no immunosuppressive therapy, and no prior similar dermatologic episodes.
elements_en.event: Probable Coxsackievirus infection in an immunocompetent adult presenting with severe vulvar ulcerations, oral ulcers, and a painful maculopapular rash on lower extremities that evolved into pustules, initially mimicking disseminated herpes simplex virus (HSV) infection and Behçet's disease. Reported in a Cureus medical case report.
elements_en.scale_impact_and_risk: Patient was afebrile and hemodynamically stable but demonstrated a marked systemic inflammatory response, including leukocytosis (white blood cell count: 21.3×10^9/L; 85% neutrophils) and elevated inflammatory markers (erythrocyte sedimentation rate: 42 mm/h; C-reactive protein: 15.4 mg/dL). Risk level not explicitly stated.
elements_en.response_status_and_uncertainty: Patient received empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics and was transitioned to valacyclovir for suspected disseminated HSV infection; leukocytosis improved rapidly with persistently sterile cultures. Subsequent serologic testing demonstrated elevated Coxsackievirus A and B titers (≥1:100), supporting an enteroviral etiology, but limitations of serologic testing preclude definitive confirmation in the absence of paired titers or lesion-based PCR. Skin biopsy demonstrated nonspecific inflammatory changes with negative direct immunofluorescence.
